license_summary.trapping_license: Trapping license required (no license required to trap groundhogs).
license_summary.trap_tags: Metallic trap tags required on every trap set for furbearers (muskrat sets exempt but tagging recommended).
license_summary.trap_check: Traps must be visited at least once every 24 hours (muskrat sets exempt).
license_summary.permission: Written landowner permission required to set traps on private land; no trapping on Division lands without a permit.
license_summary.otter_cites: River otter: CITES tagging by a Division representative required before sale or shipment out of state (302-735-3600).
license_summary.nutria_report: Nutria harvest must be reported to the Division (302-735-3600) by close of business the day after harvest; captured nutria must be killed, never released alive.
license_summary.sunday: Sunday hunting is open for all game species (2026-27 regulatory change).

seasons.notes: Red fox may be harvested with compound, recurve, longbow, crossbow, shotgun, muzzleloading rifle, or rimfire/centerfire rifle up to .25 caliber — never with handguns or straight-walled pistol-caliber rifles, and never with the aid of a light. Closed during the November youth and nonambulatory hunt and the November general firearm deer seasons. Firearm restrictions apply during deer firearms seasons. It is unlawful to kill a red fox being pursued by dogs. Chase-only (no harvest) season Oct 1-Apr 30 with deer-season closures — not modeled as take. Electronic calls may be used.

seasons.notes: Year-round (July 1–June 30). Coyotes may be harvested with compound, recurve, longbow, crossbow, shotgun, muzzleloading rifle, rimfire, or centerfire rifle up to .25 caliber — never with handguns or straight-walled pistol-caliber rifles. During any deer firearms season it is unlawful to hunt coyotes with a firearm not also legal for deer hunting. Reporting of harvested coyotes is no longer required. Hides of legally taken coyotes may be sold. Electronic calls may be used.

verification.confirmation_notes: 2026/2027 Delaware Hunting and Trapping Guide (DNREC, official eRegulations publication), pp. 39-41. Trapping: muskrat/mink/otter/raccoon/opossum/nutria Dec 1-Mar 10 (New Castle Co. embanked meadows through Mar 20); beaver Dec 1-Mar 20; red fox and coyote Nov 1-Mar 10; groundhog Jul 1-Jun 30 (no license required); no daily/possession limit for trapped furbearers; exhaustive lawful trap list. Hunting: raccoon and opossum Nov 1-Feb 28 (night light allowed; deer-season closures; raccoon chase-only Aug 1-Oct 31; opossum chase-only Mar 1-Mar 31); red fox Nov 1-Feb 28 (chase-only Oct 1-Apr 30); coyote year-round Jul 1-Jun 30; beaver Dec 1-Mar 20; raccoon special zone (private land east of Rte. 13, New Castle & Kent Cos.) open year-round for hunting and trapping; gray fox collateral take only south of the C&D Canal during red fox seasons; otter CITES tagging; nutria reporting/kill rule; coyote and gray fox reporting no longer required.
known_gaps: Opossum hunting modeled as Nov 1-Feb 28 shared with raccoon (the guide presents one hunting-season entry for the raccoon/opossum group); explicitly noted.
Deer-season-relative closures (Oct/Nov/Dec/Jan deer seasons) carried as notes; 2026/27 deer dates not extracted.
Muskrat weather-based season extension is conditional and not modeled as a fixed segment.
